review_candidates.title: Director of business intelligence & automation (RPA & AI)
review_candidates.location: San Salvador, San Salvador, El Salvador
review_candidates.description: Build the automation layer that allows AI to operate inside real companies.   MAIC is building the enterprise architecture for AI.   Enterprises already have data, systems, processes, applications, documents, and people performing thousands of interconnected actions every day. The challenge is turning all of that into an environment where AI can understand what is happening and safely take action.   That is where the Automation team comes in.   MAIC connects enterprise systems and operational data into a shared context layer. On top of that context, we build workflows, automations, applications, and AI agents that help organizations operate faster, more intelligently, and with less manual work.   As Director of Automation, you will lead the team responsible for turning enterprise context into execution.   You will own the strategy, architecture, standards, and delivery of automation across MAIC — from traditional RPA and APIs to AI agents, human-in-the-loop workflows, and intelligent enterprise automation.   This is not a traditional RPA leadership role.   We are building the infrastructure that allows AI to interact with real business systems safely and reliably.   What you will own   You will own MAIC’s automation function end-to-end.   That includes:   * Automation strategy and technical direction. * Architecture for enterprise automations and workflows. * RPA and browser automation. * API-based integrations and system actions. * AI-powered and agentic workflows. * Human-in-the-loop approval systems. * Production reliability and monitoring. * Reusable automation components and connectors. * Automation engineering standards. * Team development and technical leadership. * Delivery of customer automation projects. * Identification of new opportunities for automation across customer operations.   You will be responsible for determining not only how a process should be automated, but also which technology should automate it.   Sometimes the answer will be an API.   Sometimes it will be RPA.   Sometimes it will be an AI agent.   Sometimes it will be a deterministic workflow with human approval.   And often, it will be a combination of all four.   What would your day look like?   * Lead and grow a team of RPA, automation, and AI engineers. * Design the architecture for complex enterprise automation projects. * Review customer processes and identify opportunities for automation, AI augmentation, and process redesign. * Translate operational requirements into scalable technical solutions. * Decide when to use APIs, RPA, workflow engines, agents, or human-in-the-loop execution. * Architect automations that span multiple enterprise systems and data sources. * Build standards for production-grade automation across MAIC deployments. * Ensure automations are observable, auditable, recoverable, and secure. * Establish patterns for retries, queues, idempotency, exception handling, logging, monitoring, and escalation. * Oversee browser and desktop automations for legacy systems where modern APIs are unavailable. * Design AI-powered workflows that can interpret emails, documents, messages, forms, and unstructured information. * Define how AI agents interact with enterprise systems and what actions they are allowed to perform. * Design approval and control mechanisms for sensitive actions. * Work closely with MAIC’s Enterprise AI, Product, Data, and Engineering teams. * Connect automation workflows to MAIC’s ontology and enterprise context layer. * Create reusable actions, integrations, connectors, and automation components that can be deployed across customers. * Review technical designs and code produced by the automation engineering team. * Mentor engineers and establish strong engineering practices. * Participate directly in critical customer implementations. * Own the reliability and performance of automation running in production. * Continuously evaluate new automation and agentic technologies and determine where they fit within MAIC’s architecture.   The kind of problems you will solve   A traditional automation might say:   When an invoice arrives, enter these fields into the ERP.   At MAIC, the problem might look more like:   An invoice arrives by email.   MAIC identifies the supplier, connects the invoice to the corresponding purchase order, validates the amount against the order, checks whether the goods were received, detects a discrepancy, identifies the employee responsible for the purchase, retrieves the relevant communication history, and determines that approval is required.   An AI agent prepares the recommended action.   A human approves it.   The automation executes the appropriate action across the ERP and other systems.   Everything is logged and auditable.   That is the type of automation architecture you will help build.   What do you need to be successful?   * 7+ years of experience in software engineering, automation, RPA, systems integration, enterprise technology, or related fields. * Experience leading engineers or technical delivery teams. * Strong hands-on understanding of RPA and enterprise automation. * Experience with tools such as UiPath, Power Automate, Automation Anywhere, Robocorp, Playwright, Selenium, or similar technologies. * Strong software engineering fundamentals. * Experience with Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, Java, or similar languages. * Strong understanding of REST APIs, webhooks, authentication, databases, and enterprise integrations. * Experience designing integrations across complex enterprise systems. * Strong understanding of SQL and relational databases. * Experience designing distributed or asynchronous systems. * Understanding of queues, retries, idempotency, state management, and fault tolerance. * Experience operating automations or integrations in production environments. * Ability to design systems that are reliable, observable, secure, and maintainable. * Strong architectural judgment. * Ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and business leaders. * Experience working directly with customers or enterprise stakeholders. * Ability to understand complex business processes and translate them into technical architectures. * Strong leadership, mentoring, and problem-solving skills.   Strong pluses   * Experience building AI agents or LLM-powered applications. * Experience with tool calling, MCP, or agent orchestration. * Experience with intelligent document processing. * Experience with OCR, computer vision, or multimodal AI. * Experience with process mining. * Experience with workflow orchestration platforms. * Experience integrating SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce, ServiceNow, or similar enterprise platforms. * Experience with event-driven architectures. * Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP. * Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, or distributed systems. * Experience designing human-in-the-loop systems. * Understanding of enterprise identity, RBAC, permissions, security, and audit trails. * Familiarity with knowledge graphs, ontologies, or enterprise semantic models.   Leadership expectations   This role is not only about managing a team.   You should be able to go deep technically when necessary.   You should be comfortable reviewing an architecture in the morning, debugging a failed production automation in the afternoon, working through a customer’s operational process with their leadership team, and then helping an engineer design a better implementation.   You will establish the engineering culture of the Automation team.   We expect you to:   * Set a high technical bar. * Build systems for reuse rather than one-off scripts. * Push the team toward API-first automation where appropriate. * Know when RPA is the right tool and when it is not. * Design automations for failure, not just the happy path. * Treat monitoring and observability as part of the product. * Build security and permissions into the architecture. * Keep humans in control of sensitive decisions. * Help engineers grow technically and professionally. * Turn lessons from individual customer implementations into reusable MAIC platform capabilities.   Why this role matters   AI can generate an answer.   Enterprise AI needs to do much more.   It needs to understand the organization, know what actions are possible, respect permissions and business rules, interact with existing systems, recover when something fails, and know when a human needs to make the final decision.   MAIC’s context layer gives AI an understanding of the enterprise.   The Automation team gives it the ability to act.   As Director of Automation, you will build and lead that capability.   By being part of MAIC   You will work on the intersection of enterprise software, AI, automation, and real-world operations.   You will build systems that interact with the core infrastructure companies use every day.   You will lead engineers working across traditional automation, enterprise integrations, intelligent workflows, and AI agents.   And you will help define what automation looks like in a world where software no longer just follows predefined steps — it can understand context and participate intelligently in business processes.   You will lead the team responsible for turning enterprise AI from intelligence into action.

review_candidates.title: Vice President, Engineering
review_candidates.description: The Opportunity Company, Department: Emera Inc, Corporate Development. Location: Halifax, NS Closing Date: October 7, 2026 Emera is a leading North American provider of energy services headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia with $43B in total assets. Emera delivers safe, clean, and reliable energy to customers through investments in regulated electric and natural gas utilities, and related businesses and assets Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Corporate Development & CEO Emera Energy, the Vice President, Engineering will play a key role in advancing Emera’s growth strategy. The Vice President is critical to ensure that the technical capabilities required to deliver complex transmission infrastructure are proactively planned, effectively deployed, and consistently aligned to project execution; reducing delivery risk and enabling successful, on-time outcomes. The role is accountable for the strategic oversight, planning, and deployment of specialized technical capabilities required to deliver large-scale transmission infrastructure projects. Additionally, the VP will ensure the right engineering, technical, and specialist resources are in place at the right time to ultimately enable safe, cost-effective, and on-schedule execution of transmission line development and construction. The VP operates at the intersection of business development, engineering, project delivery, workforce strategy, and external partnerships, with a core mandate to de-risk execution through proactive capability planning and technical oversight. Accountabilities: Partnering with business development, lead the development of an integrated resource strategy for transmission projects, including engineering, environmental, regulatory, and construction-related technical roles Ensure technical excellence, consistency, and quality standards across internal teams and external partners Define and oversee a Build–Buy–Borrow model to balance internal capability, external expertise, and contractor support Ensure time-phased resource plans align with project lifecycle stages (development, permitting, engineering, construction, commissioning) Provide leadership oversight for critical technical disciplines, including: Transmission line engineering (civil, electrical, structural) Environmental and permitting expertise Geotechnical and survey specialists Construction and commissioning technical supervisors Establish and manage strategic partnerships with EPC firms, engineering consultants, and contractors Ensure clear accountability for delivery of technical resources across partners Lead integrated workforce planning forums across internal and external stakeholders Embed resource-related performance expectations into contracts and agreements, underpinned by commercial acumen Collaborate with partners to determine capabilities and the clear delineation of technical roles and responsibilities within JV structures Ensure disciplined integration and clear accountability across technical interfaces spanning JV partners, EP/EPC contractors and delivery teams Support the alignment of technical risk ownership and performance accountability within JV agreements and contractual frameworks Ensure technical strategies are aligned with Indigenous partnerships, regulatory obligations and broader impacted group commitments Leadership: Provide strategic leadership in global OEM engagement and supply chain positioning for critical technologies (HVDC), including early supplier engagement, capacity assurance and integration with JV commercial and delivery models Provide leadership in the establishment and alignment of JV operating models and technical accountability structures Provide technical leadership to inform early-stage project development, enhancing commercial viability, constructability and execution certainty Lead a team of specialist resources and partner closely with the GM, Business Development and/or other business partners on business development proposals Champion a culture of safety, quality and accountability across all partners and activities Communicate complex workforce and technical issues in a clear and concise manner Has the ability to elevate issues early and frames options, risk and trade-offs to make informed decisions Advise executives and influence investment decisions Competencies: Strategic Orientation: Translates project and corporate strategy into actionable capability plans Execution Focus: Drives delivery through disciplined planning and proactive risk management Influence & Partnership: Builds alignment across internal leaders and external partners Decision Making Under Uncertainty: Balances speed, cost, and quality in dynamic project environments Risk Management: Anticipates and mitigates workforce-related delivery risks Operational Excellence: Ensures consistent standards and continuous improvement across technical teams Qualifications & Experience: Relevant Engineering Designation, with 12+ years of experience in large-scale infrastructure, utilities, or energy projects Must have proven executive level experience in the design, development, delivery and operation of high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems. Experience with subsea cable projects would be advantageous Significant experience in transmission, power systems, or major capital project delivery Proven leadership in managing multidisciplinary engineering and technical teams Experience working with EPC contractors, engineering firms, and complex vendor ecosystems Strong understanding of project lifecycle phases and workforce implications Experience in resource planning, workforce strategy, or operational scaling is highly preferred The perks of joining our team? We offer: Health & Wellbeing: A comprehensive benefits plan, 24/7 access to virtual health care services for you and your family through Dialogue, access to a free on-site fitness centre, Employee and Family Assistance Program, parental leave top-up plan and wellness benefits. Grow Your Career: Opportunities to advance within and between our operating businesses, a focus on employee development and available sponsored education programs. Community Engagement & Care: Corporate investments in the places where our people live and work, mentoring opportunities, fundraising-matching & volunteer programs, and scholarships for children of employees. Competitive Compensation: A comprehensive benefits plan, short-term and long-term incentive plans, and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan. Inclusion at Emera : As one of Atlantic Canada’s largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community. Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation. review_candidates.title: Vice President, Critical Infrastructure Programs
review_candidates.description: About Day & Zimmermann No matter the mission, SOC delivers! We provide a full suite of integrated solutions that support security and protection needs in high-threat environments across the globe. Our reputation as a responsive, agile and trusted partner precedes us. Still not convinced? We’re trusted by the U.S. Government and other commercial clients to detect and deter the full spectrum of threats in support of national security interests. As a Day & Zimmermann company, we have the strength to achieve mission objectives in any corner of the world. Come join in on our purpose – We put people to work, we protect American freedoms, and we help our customers power and improve the world! https://www.soc-usa.com/about-us About The Opportunity Join SOC LLC as the Vice President of Critical Infrastructure Programs where you will play a pivotal leadership role in steering the strategic direction, operational excellence, and financial performance of a vital business unit. This unit serves diverse markets including the Department of Energy (DOE), commercial data centers, and related sectors, empowering you to contribute to the security and sustainability of essential infrastructure. Your leadership will be instrumental in expanding business opportunities and fostering robust partnerships with government entities and private clients alike. You are entrusted with cultivating high-performing teams, enhancing organizational capabilities, and ensuring that our services consistently meet or exceed rigorous standards. This role offers a unique platform to impact national infrastructure resilience while building a legacy of innovation and growth within the critical infrastructure landscape. In this capacity, you will oversee multi-million dollar budgets and large-scale operations, emphasizing strategic pursuits and efficient program execution. Your ability to lead through complexity and change will be vital, as you align cross-functional teams to a shared vision of security, excellence, and client responsiveness. SOC LLC values diverse perspectives and invites candidates who bring a collaborative spirit and a commitment to ethical leadership. As the Vice President, Critical Infrastructure Programs, here is the work you'll do: Develop and drive comprehensive business strategies that encompass DOE-funded projects and relevant commercial opportunities. Translate these strategies into actionable plans that deliver measurable results and sustainable growth. Lead and mentor multi-disciplinary teams, including Program and Account Managers, to uphold operational excellence and customer satisfaction, ensuring alignment with stakeholder expectations and contractual obligations. Implement robust governance practices by actively participating in DOE oversight boards and facilitating critical decision-making processes that shape project outcomes. Actively engage in business development processes by contributing to capture management, pricing strategies, and talent acquisition to secure and expand contract portfolios. Foster enduring client relationships through frequent engagement, needs assessments, and proactive resolution of challenges to maintain trust and deepen partnerships. Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance cost efficiency, operational workflows, and employee engagement across all managed programs. Provide transparent and timely communication of program status, risks, and opportunities to executive leadership and key stakeholders. This role is for you if you have these skills: Demonstrated leadership in managing complex government contracts and programs, particularly within DOE markets, showcasing the ability to navigate regulatory environments and contractual nuances. Proficient in leading diverse teams by fostering a culture of accountability, motivation, and professional growth, ensuring that all leaders and staff are equipped to meet evolving business needs. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret and apply government regulations to business practices, developing compliant policies and procedures that facilitate operational success. Strategic thinker with a track record of designing and implementing initiatives that align with organizational mission, stimulate workforce potential, and uphold high ethical standards. Exceptional communication skills capable of conveying complex technical and business concepts clearly and persuasively to a variety of audiences, facilitating collaboration and informed decision-making. And If You Have These Qualifications High school diploma or GED required; Bachelor's degree in arts, sciences, or related fields preferred. Advanced degrees are advantageous to support strategic leadership responsibilities. Minimum of 15 years extensive experience within government program environments such as DOE, DOD, and DOS, with at least 7 years in senior management roles overseeing substantial teams and budgets. Proven financial stewardship with responsibility for budgets exceeding $40 million annually, demonstrating fiscal discipline and resource optimization. Experience managing large-scale integrated security and emergency services programs involving workforces of 3,000 or more employees, with a focus on ensuring operational readiness and compliance. Specialized knowledge and practical experience managing Safeguards, Security, and Emergency Management at DOE sites, ensuring alignment with federal mandates and site-specific requirements. In compliance with this state’s pay transparency laws, the salary range for this role is $174,080 - $304,640. This is not a guarantee of compensation or salary, as the final offer amount may vary based on factors including but not limited to experience and geographic location. (The specific programs and options available to an employee may vary depending on date of hire, schedule type, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements). We care about our employees, and it shows. Our staff receive a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical/Rx, dental and vision coverage; life, AD&D and disability insurance; flexible spending accounts; 100% paid maternity leave for up to 12 weeks, parental leave, family leave, other paid time off; voluntary benefits and discount programs to meet our employees’ individual needs including pet insurance for our furry family members!
